Srikant vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. on 17
January, 2023

Author: Rajesh Singh Chauhan
Bench: Rajesh Singh Chauhan
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Court No. - 11
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 14348 of 2022
Applicant :- Srikant

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Subodh Kumar Pandey,Ramakar Shukla Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.
Heard Sri Ramakar Shukla, learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.

It has been contended by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is in jail since 2.10.2022 in Case Crime No. 234 of 2022 u/s 498A, 323, 306 IPC & section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Kotwali Sadar, District Lakhimpur Kheri.
It has been submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case as he has not committed any offence as alleged.
Attention has been drawn towards the impugned F.I.R. wherein the date of incident has been indicated as 6.3.2022, however, the F.I.R. has been lodged on 19.3.2022 i.e. after the delay of 13 days.

The aforesaid inordinate delay of 13 days has not been explained whereas in view of present facts and circumstances the aforesaid delay must be explained properly inasmuch as the victim (since deceased) died in the house of her parents.
The cause of death is hanging.
The present Srikant vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

1 applicant is husband of the victim (since deceased), therefore, he must have been informed about the suicide of his wife but in the present case after the suicide of his wife the inquest was prepared wherein all five 'Panchs' are the family members of his wife.
As per inquest report the death appears to be suicide.
Thereafter wife of the present applicant has been cremated and no such information has been given to the present applicant.
This is not a case of the informant / complainant that the information of death of the wife of the applicant has been informed to him but he or his family members did not turn up.

Even in the statement of the complainant / informant and other family members of the wife of the applicant, no such allegation has been levelled, meaning thereby the information of the death of the wife of the present applicant has not been given to him.

Learned counsel for the applicant has drawn attention of this Court towards Annexure no. 6 which is an order being passed by the Principal Judge, Family Court, Shahjahanpur whereby the present applicant was awarded decree of divorce from his first wife on 17.9.2017.
As per Sri Shukla, after getting divorce from his wife the present applicant got married with the victim (since deceased).
However, on such marriage the family members of his wife were not happy, therefore, they were compelling her to get divorce from the present applicant but she was not agreeable on that.

Annexure no. 6 and Annexure no. 7 is a copy of complaint of his wife filed before the Court of F.T.C.,
Shahjahanpur bearing Case No. 362 of 2021 (Sneha Rastogi vs. Saurabh Rastogi & others) against the family members of wherein she has stated that after her marriage with the present applicant her family members are harassing her, however, she is happily living with her husband, the present applicant.

entities.text: Sneha Rastogi vs. Saurabh Rastogi & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The aforesaid complaint has been filed on 4.8.2021.

As per Sri Shukla just after knowing the fact that after the death of wife of the applicant she has been cremated, he filed an application / complaint before the Superintendent of Police, Lakhimpur Kheri on 1.4.2022 (Annexure no. 8) making request that he may be provided proper justice.

He has further submitted that when the family members of the wife of the applicant were not happy with the marriage of the victim (since deceased) with the present applicant, no question arises to demand dowry as the allegation of demanding dowry or torturing are false and misconceived.
Since the wife of the present applicant died in the house of her parents on 6.3.2022, therefore, so as to save their skin they lodged false and fabricated F.I.R. on 19.3.2022.
As a matter of fact the present applicant is himself aggrieved from the manner the information of death of his wife has been suppressed and concealed from him.
He has further submitted that the charge-sheet has been filed in the present case.

The learned counsel for the applicant has given an undertaking on behalf of applicant that the applicant shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with the trial proceedings and shall abide by all terms and conditions of bail, if granted.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the wife of the present applicant has committed suicide after being fed up from the behaviour of the present applicant, therefore, he is not entitled for bail.

However, on being confronted on the point as to why the information of the death of the wife of the present applicant has not been given to him and also about the complaint being filed by the wife of the applicant against her family members, learned AGA has submitted that those facts may be verified during the course of the course of the trial.

Without entering into the merits of the case and considering the arguments of learned counsel for the parties, contents and allegations of the F.I.R., the complaint being filed by the wife of the applicant against her family members, there is no explanation on inordinate delay of 13 days in lodging the F.I.R. and the undertaking given on behalf of the applicant that he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate in the trial proceedings, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail in this case.

Let the applicant Srikant, involved in aforesaid case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
(v) The applicant shall not leave the country without permission of the Court concerned.
Before parting with it is expected that the trial shall be concluded with expedition.
Further, the learned trial court may take all coercive measures as per law if either of the parties do not co-operate in the trial properly.
The learned trial court shall fix short dates to ensure that trial is concluded at the earliest.

. 
(Rajesh Singh Chauhan, J.) Order Date :- 17.1.2023 Om  Srikant vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.
